title: G1 C11 · Fitness and Cardiac Health

questions.q: Fitness and health have different meanings. State the meaning of fitness.
questions.explain: Fitness means being able to do physical activities well without getting tired too quickly.

questions.q: Fitness and health have different meanings. State the meaning of health.
questions.explain: Health means being free from disease and illness.

questions.q: Blood flows to all parts of the body. Name two substances it brings to cells.
questions.explain: Blood brings oxygen and glucose to our cells. The cells use them in respiration to release energy.

questions.q: Blood flows to all parts of the body. Name two substances it takes away from cells.
questions.explain: Blood takes carbon dioxide and other wastes away from our cells.

questions.q: Blood has four parts. Name the part that carries oxygen.
questions.explain: Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body.

questions.q: Name the part of blood that helps blood to clot.
questions.explain: Platelets help blood to clot. A clot seals a cut and stops the bleeding.

questions.q: Name the part of blood that destroys bacteria.
questions.explain: White blood cells destroy bacteria and other germs. They help the body fight infection.

questions.q: Name the part of blood that carries food substances and carbon dioxide.
questions.explain: Plasma is the liquid part of blood. It carries dissolved food substances and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: A cut keeps bleeding for a long time. Identify which part of blood is too low.
questions.explain: Platelets help blood to clot. If there are too few platelets, a cut keeps bleeding for a long time.

questions.q: After surgery, a patient has many more white blood cells. Suggest a reason.
questions.explain: White blood cells fight germs. A big rise in white blood cells is a sign that the body is fighting an infection.

questions.q: Blood low in oxygen returns from the body. Name where it enters first.
questions.explain: Blood low in oxygen returns from the body along veins into the right side of the heart.

questions.q: The right side of the heart pumps blood out. State where this blood goes.
questions.explain: The right side of the heart pumps blood low in oxygen to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen.

questions.q: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs. State where this blood goes next.
questions.explain: Blood that has picked up oxygen in the lungs flows back to the left side of the heart.

questions.q: The left side of the heart pumps blood out. State where this blood goes.
choices: back to the left side of the heart
questions.explain: The left side of the heart pumps blood rich in oxygen to the rest of the body.

questions.q: Blood has just entered the left side of the heart. Name where it came from.
questions.explain: Blood enters the left side of the heart from the lungs, after it has picked up oxygen there.

questions.q: An artery has a thick muscular wall. Explain why.
choices: to carry blood to the heart
to cope with high blood pressure
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood pumped out of the heart at high pressure. Their thick, muscular walls can cope with this high pressure.

questions.q: A vein has valves inside it. Explain why.
choices: to cope with high blood pressure
questions.explain: Blood in veins flows slowly at low pressure. Valves stop the blood from flowing backwards.

questions.q: Describe the wall of a capillary.
questions.explain: The wall of a capillary is only one cell thick. This lets substances pass easily between the blood and the cells.

questions.q: Name the blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart.
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins carry blood back to the heart.

questions.q: Name the blood vessel that carries blood back to the heart.
questions.explain: Veins carry blood back to the heart. Arteries carry blood away from the heart.

questions.q: Gases pass between blood and body cells. Name the blood vessel where this happens.
questions.explain: Substances pass between the blood and body cells through capillaries. Their walls are only one cell thick.

questions.q: Cholesterol can build up inside arteries. Name the fatty deposits it forms.
questions.explain: Cholesterol builds up inside arteries as fatty deposits called plaques. Plaques make the arteries narrower.

questions.q: An artery to the heart muscle is blocked. Explain why this causes a heart attack.
choices: the heart muscle gets less oxygen
the heart muscle gets more oxygen
questions.explain: The heart muscle gets oxygen from the blood in its own arteries. If one is blocked, part of the heart muscle gets less oxygen and is damaged. This is a heart attack.

questions.q: An artery to the brain is blocked by plaques. Name the condition this causes.
questions.explain: A blocked artery to the brain stops oxygen reaching part of the brain. This is a stroke.

questions.q: Pulse rate counts pulses in one minute. State how it compares with heart rate.
questions.explain: Each heart beat makes one pulse in the arteries. So the pulse rate is the same as the heart rate.

questions.q: Each heart beat gives a pulse in one type of blood vessel. Name this blood vessel.
questions.explain: Each heart beat pushes a surge of blood along the arteries. This surge is felt as a pulse.

questions.q: Pulse rate goes up during exercise. Explain why.
choices: the body needs to cool down
questions.explain: During exercise the muscles need more oxygen and glucose for respiration. The heart beats faster to deliver them, so the pulse rate goes up.

questions.q: Three pulse readings add up to 210 beats/min. Calculate the average pulse rate.
questions.explain: Average pulse rate = total ÷ number of readings = 210 ÷ 3 = 70 beats/min.

questions.q: Three pulse readings have an average of 60 beats/min. Calculate their total.
questions.explain: Total = average × number of readings = 60 × 3 = 180 beats/min.

questions.q: Four students have different resting pulse rates. Identify the fittest student.
questions.explain: A fitter heart pumps more blood with each beat, so it needs to beat less often at rest. The lowest resting pulse rate, 60 beats/min, shows the fittest student.

questions.q: Two people do the same exercise. Predict whose pulse rate returns to resting first.
questions.explain: A fitter person's heart recovers more quickly after exercise. So their pulse rate returns to resting first.

questions.q: Name the part of a joint that joins bone to bone.
questions.explain: A ligament joins bone to bone at a joint.

questions.q: Name the part of a joint that joins muscle to bone.
questions.explain: A tendon joins muscle to bone. When the muscle pulls, the tendon pulls the bone.

questions.q: Name the part of a joint that absorbs shock.
questions.explain: Cartilage covers the ends of the bones in a joint. It absorbs shock and stops the bones rubbing together.

questions.q: In a joint, the bones are forced out of their places. Name this problem.
questions.explain: When the bones in a joint are forced out of their places, the joint is dislocated. This is a dislocation.

questions.q: A ligament is stretched too far or torn. Name this problem.
questions.explain: A sprain is when a ligament is stretched too far or torn.

questions.q: Bones become weak and break easily. Name this condition.
questions.explain: Osteoporosis is a condition in which bones become weak and break easily.

questions.q: A person has arthritis. Describe what has happened to the joints.
choices: the bones are out of place
questions.explain: In arthritis the joints become swollen and painful, and they are hard to move.

questions.q: Osteoporosis is caused by a lack of two substances. Name these substances.
questions.explain: Bones need calcium to stay strong, and vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium. A lack of both can cause osteoporosis.
